title: SSE capability discovery, priority window, and function-call gating for streaming compatibility bridge
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Problem: Legacy clients and third-party middleware expect different streaming encodings (jsonl, length-prefixed, chunked-delta) and have varying tolerance for backpressure. We need a single SSE-based compatibility bridge that negotiates capabilities at handshake time, exposes a priority window for important fragments, and guarantees function-call atomicity across reconnects. Goal: Implement a wire-level capability-discovery handshake plus a priority leasing mechanism and function-call gating semantics so that: 1) modern clients can opt into compact delta framing and prioritized fragments, 2) legacy clients continue to receive jsonl or length-prefixed streams, and 3) function-call events are delivered atomically or replay-safe during reconnection.
acceptance_criteria: Capability discovery header and first-event handshake implemented: server emits 'capabilities' event with supported encodings and priority-window semantics
Client negotiation: server honors 'Prefer-Stream-Encoding' and 'Prefer-Stream-Compat' request headers to select encoding/mode
Priority window: server implements a three-tier window (high/normal/low) and honors client-supplied backpressure hints for lease sizes
Function-call gating: function call boundaries are checkpointed and replay-safe so a reconnecting client will not see partial function-call payloads
Compatibility shim: server can transcode length-prefixed -> jsonl and vice-versa for legacy clients with <5% p99 latency regression under typical load
Automated tests for handshake, priority preemption, and reconnect replay safety added and passing in CI
Docs and SDK updates: streaming spec, example client handshake, and migration guidance published
implementation_notes: Handshake sequence: client includes 'Prefer-Stream-Encoding: jsonl|length-prefixed|delta' and 'Prefer-Stream-Compat: legacy|modern' headers. On new session server sends initial 'event: capabilities' with capabilities JSON (compact string encoded) followed by an 'event: ack' confirming chosen mode.
Wire fields: use 'X-Redwood-Stream-Seq' as monotonic sequence id (server-assigned) and 'X-Redwood-Stream-Lease' events to indicate priority-window grants
Backpressure tokens: server will issue time-limited leases (lease_id + credits) via 'lease' events. Clients should decrement credits and emit 'heartbeat' or 'lease-return' when underutilized.

Priority window semantics: high-priority fragments bypass normal batching and are emitted immediately but consume from a separate high-lease. Normal/low fragments share a pooled lease to preserve throughput.

Function-call atomicity: on function-call start server emits 'event: func_start' with id and idempotency token. All function-call content arrives as 'event: func_payload' chunks. Server emits 'event: func_commit' when call completes. On reconnect clients acknowledge last seen func_commit id. If a client reconnects mid-function, server will transparently re-emit func_payloads from last committed checkpoint or provide a compact snapshot reference for large payloads.

Compatibility shim: add a thin transcoder component in edge layer that translates between encodings. For legacy clients set 'Prefer-Stream-Compat: legacy' to enable the shim. The shim should preserve sequence ids and function-call tokens to maintain idempotency guarantees.
Observability: emit metrics for handshake success rate, average lease utilization, high-priority preemption count, and function-call replay rate. Add traces for handshake negotiation path.
Security: handshake must respect SSO token and RBAC. Do not leak capability details for customers with restricted feature sets. KMS-backed tokens for lease signing if running in Private mode.
test_plan: Unit tests for handshake parser and negotiation state machine (simulate all header permutations)
Integration test: two client types (legacy jsonl, modern delta) join same model stream; verify both get consistent final outputs
Reconnect fuzz: force mid-function disconnects and verify client sees either full re-emission from checkpoint or compact snapshot reference; assert no duplicated function_commit events
Load test: measure p50/p95/p99 latency with and without transcoder shim enabled; confirm <5% p99 regression for typical request patterns
Backpressure test: simulate client that pauses consumption and verify server issues lease-return and reclaims high-priority window as expected
End-to-end SDK tests: example Node and Python clients exercise header negotiation and lease renewal APIs
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gate behind 'sse.capability-discovery' and 'sse.priority-lease' (default off in prod)
Stage 1 (internal): enable in staging and run synthetic cross-compat tests for 48 hours
Stage 2 (canary): enable for 2% of traffic on hosted API for 72 hours and monitor handshake metrics and function-call replay counts
Stage 3 (broader rollout): 25% -> 75% -> 100% over 2 weeks, with rollback on handshake-failure spike or >1% function-call replay errors
Migration docs: provide sample code for clients to set 'Prefer-Stream-Encoding' and how to fall back to legacy mode if unsupported
